title: Harness: manna board mutations race — unlocked read-modify-write silently loses concurrent writes
description: Confirmed live 2026-07-22: lane9's manna done on mn-14b8c0 was silently reverted to open by a near-concurrent CLI mutation. Root cause store.rs:165-210 update_issue (and delete_issue; every mutating verb routes through them): load_issues runs with NO cross-process lock; the exclusive lock is taken on each writer's OWN temp file (store.rs:194), which excludes nobody; second rename wins with a stale snapshot, reverting the first write. append_issue locks the real issues file but an append can still be lost to a concurrent update's rename. Fix: one sidecar lockfile (.manna/board.lock) acquired exclusively around the FULL load-mutate-write-rename in every mutating path incl. append; add a cross-PROCESS concurrency test (the existing 10-thread test covers only concurrent appends in-process). Multi-agent parallel writes are the design case; the board that cannot lie must not lose writes.

description: WHAT: _counsel_latest_log (lib/counsel.sh:97) follows tmp/logs/latest via readlink and reads the resolved session dir and log file unconfined — an absolute or dot-dot symlink target (committable in git) reaches arbitrary local files, whose tail then lands in a counsel brief on disk and in a model call. Auto-relit + hook inject make this triggerable by merely opening a session in a hostile repo. FIX: realpath -e both the resolved session dir AND the final log path; require both under realpath of the project root; otherwise emit the declarative unavailable line. Regression test: symlink escape attempt yields the unavailable receipt, never file content. SOURCE: automated security review 2026-07-27, MEDIUM, severity raised by the automation chain.

title: zpc: mine past corrections into preference lessons
description: WHAT: zpc harvest --corrections — scan session transcripts (agent-do sessions FTS) for user-correction moments (too wordy / not what I asked / try again / interrupts), extract pair (what the assistant did -> what Erik said), write dated preference lessons with verbatim quote receipts to the user-global zpc layer, tagged preference,mined, dedup by content-hash id. Inject's global slice then delivers them to every session; challenge/retract machinery applies. Flags only, no new verbs. WHY: don't classify intent forward, mine misses backward — receipts over guesses.

title: hooks: one-keystroke correction channel (w/d/s)
description: WHAT: UserPromptSubmit hook matching EXACT single-key prompts — w (too wordy: re-answer kernel-first), d (go deeper on the last answer), s (re-answer via subtraction form). Expands the key into explicit correction context for the model AND appends a receipt {ts,key,cwd} to ~/.agent-do/zpc/corrections.jsonl. Exact-match command vocabulary, not prose guessing. Kill switch AGENT_DO_CORRECTION_KEYS=0. Registered via install.sh spec list. WHY: correction must cost one keystroke; each press is intent data with a receipt.

title: CLAUDE.md: kernel-first reply contract (expansion on pull)
description: WHAT: one law in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md Say the Thing section: default reply = answer in ~5 lines + load-bearing specifics; detail only on pull. Structure beats style instructions because instructions lose to session momentum. Executed directly by orchestrator.

title: zpc: inject --preferences — global slice with no store required
description: WHAT: flag on inject rendering ONLY the user-global slice (preference+technique lessons, patterns-free), <=2000 chars with the standard truncation marker, works when NO .zpc store exists (skip ensure_zpc; empty output + exit 0 when global file absent). No new verbs. WHY: Erik directive 2026-07-28: global preferences follow me everywhere.

title: hooks: auto-init .zpc in git repos + inject preferences everywhere
description: WHAT: (1) SessionStart (claude + codex) auto-runs zpc init when cwd is inside a git repo with no .zpc up-tree; silent, bounded 3s, kill switch AGENT_DO_ZPC_AUTOINIT=0. (2) When no store/records exist, hook embeds 'zpc inject --preferences' output so global preferences reach every session anywhere. WHY: Erik directive 2026-07-28: every project gets a store by default; preferences are user-level, not project-level.

title: zpc: init --store-only — a store without the repo edits
description:
WHAT: add --store-only to 'zpc init'. Creates .zpc/{memory,team,.state} + data files and updates the global project index; SKIPS the .gitignore append (integration.sh:522-529) and the instruction-file write/append (integration.sh:555-573). Keep init's leak protection without touching a tracked file by writing '.zpc/' into .git/info/exclude when the repo does not already ignore it. Must appear in cmd_init's --help usage line: the hooks gate on that string.

WHY: mn-1fb38d auto-runs init at every SessionStart in every git worktree. Plain init is not store-only — verified 2026-07-28 in a scratch repo: after 'agent-do zpc init', .gitignore gained the .zpc/ block and a pre-existing AGENTS.md gained a trailing '@.zpc/zpc-brain.md' line. A silent session-start hook may not edit tracked files in a repo it does not own, least of all an agent instruction file.

STATE: hooks/claude/agent-do-session-start.sh and hooks/codex/agent-do-session-start.py (commit 801268d) already implement auto-init and gate it POSITIVELY on the literal string '--store-only' appearing in 'zpc init --help'. init's arg loop swallows unknown flags (integration.sh:485), so an ungated call would silently run the invasive path. Until this ships the gate stays shut: no auto-init, no repo mutation, and the preferences half of mn-1fb38d is unaffected and already live. Shipping this flag turns auto-init on with no further hook change.

title: hooks: session memory is cwd-scoped — a subdir session misses its own project's store
description:
WHAT: both SessionStart hooks resolve the store as literally $CWD/.zpc (hooks/claude/agent-do-session-start.sh append_zpc_memory, hooks/codex/agent-do-session-start.py zpc()). zpc itself resolves a store by walking UP from cwd (tools/agent-zpc/lib/common.sh:resolve_zpc_dir). So a session started in a subdirectory of a repo whose store lives at the toplevel does not see that store at all.

RECEIPT (2026-07-28, real dispatcher): scratch repo with 1 recorded lesson at toplevel; hook run with cwd=<repo>/src/deep emitted the global ZPC Preferences slice, not the project's memory and not the advisory. Same result on both hooks.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: not a regression — before mn-1fb38d a subdir session got no ZPC section whatsoever, so preferences are strictly an improvement. But auto-init (mn-1fb38d + mn-39a482) means stores now exist in every git repo, which makes cwd-scoping the thing standing between a subdir session and memory that demonstrably exists two directories up. Monorepo and package-subdir sessions are the common case.

FIX SHAPE: resolve the store root by walking cwd up to the git toplevel (auto-init already does exactly this walk), then feed that root to the records check and to inject's cwd instead of $CWD. Constraint: the record-bearing path must stay byte-identical for sessions started AT the store root — that equivalence is pinned by mn-1fb38d's verification and is the regression guard for this change (run the orig-vs-new context diff on a repo with records).

NOT CLAIMED BY LANE 22: out of that lane's pinned contract; filed rather than folded in, because it changes store resolution on the exact path mn-1fb38d had to keep byte-stable.

title: zpc: bound resolve_zpc_dir's upward walk (toplevel, HOME floor, ownership)
description: WHAT: tools/agent-zpc/lib/common.sh resolve_zpc_dir walks up unbounded, same class as the hook finding (mn-90eb96 security rider): from a scratch cwd it can adopt a planted /tmp/.zpc or another user's store as the project store — every zpc command would then read AND write attacker-controlled memory. FIX: stop at git toplevel when inside a worktree; never ascend past $HOME (probe $HOME last); outside $HOME with no worktree, probe cwd only; trust only stores owned by the current uid (stat -f %u on darwin). Regression: planted-store matrix + existing store resolution unchanged. SOURCE: automated security review 2026-07-28, MEDIUM.

title: SECURITY: hook store walk was unbounded — planted store could inject trusted memory
description:
SEVERITY: local prompt injection + write into an attacker-controlled directory. Introduced by 051bb1e (mn-90eb96), fixed by 6245645. Never shipped in a release; window was within one session.

VULNERABILITY: both SessionStart hooks resolved a zpc store by walking cwd upward with no ceiling and no ownership check. A session opened anywhere under a world-writable directory (macOS /tmp is sticky but world-writable) would discover a .zpc planted above it and embed its lessons under the heading 'This project's recorded memory. Read it before coding' — attacker-controlled text in the trusted region of the agent's context, unattended, at session start. The same resolution chose the write-nudge baseline's location, so the hook also wrote into that directory.

REPRODUCED 2026-07-28 before fixing: store planted at /tmp/<dir>/.zpc with a lesson whose takeaway was a marker string; session cwd two levels below; marker appeared in additionalContext under the ZPC Project Memory heading on the claude hook. Confirmed zero after the fix on both hooks.

FIX (6245645): (1) ceiling — a git worktree stops at its toplevel, a cwd under $HOME stops at $HOME, a cwd outside both probes only itself; a worktree rooted above $HOME does not lift the $HOME ceiling. (2) ownership — a discovered store is used only when st_uid == getuid(), following symlinks (stat -L / Path.stat) so a .zpc symlinked elsewhere is judged by what it resolves to. A store not owned by the current uid ends the walk rather than being climbed past.

TESTS: tests/test_hook_store_resolution.py covers planted-store-not-discovered (with and without a worktree below it), the $HOME ceiling, and unowned-store-refused on both hooks with the uid spoofed, since an unprivileged test cannot chown. In-boundary behavior unchanged: deep subdirectory still reaches its own project memory; session at the store root byte-identical to pre-lane.

NOTE FOR THE ZPC SURFACE: zpc's own resolve_zpc_dir (tools/agent-zpc/lib/common.sh) is still an unbounded, ownership-blind walk. That is lower risk because it runs when a human invokes it rather than silently at session start, but 'agent-do zpc inject' run by hand from /tmp has the same exposure. Worth a decision by the zpc owner: bound it, or document that it trusts cwd's ancestry.

title: DREAM: agent-be as a second face on agent-do
description: Split the vocabulary without splitting the repo: an agent-be entry point (symlink, argv0-aware dispatch) exposing only the identity domain, with 'domain: be' tags in the one registry on zpc/context/sessions; manna and coord deliberately unclassified until usage shows which face reaches for them. Do-tools touch the world (browse, db, render, slack); be-tools are memory and judgment. Erik 2026-07-28: 'agent-do should feel pure (interacting with the world via structured discipline).' Orchestrator recommendation was yes-minimal; Erik parked it. Falsifier if built: nothing invokes agent-be within a month (receipts) = vanity alias, drop it. Reopen trigger: agent-do gets real public distribution, which forces the question anyway. DECIDE LATER — no agent executes this.

title: install.sh: warn when an installed wrapper has no settings registration
description: WHAT: install.sh installs hook wrappers unconditionally (step 4) but only merges settings.json when --register-hooks / interactive-yes. A run without the flag therefore leaves wrappers on disk for hooks that never fire, silently — this happened live 2026-07-28: correction-keys wrapper installed 13:19, never registered, w/d/s dead with no signal. FIX: at the end of a run, compare installed wrapper names against the registered set in settings.json and print a loud line naming each dead wrapper plus the exact re-run command. Read-only check, no auto-write. SOURCE: orchestrator verification 2026-07-28.

title: manna: dreams are inert until Erik converts them
description: WHAT: (1) 'claim' refuses type:dream with exit 2 and a message pointing at conversion (no status change, nothing written); (2) dreams STAY VISIBLE everywhere they are today — list, context, status — Erik's ruling 2026-07-28: 'I don't want them hidden from work lists, I want them visible and denied without conversion'; visibility is the point, the refusal is the gate; (3) render dreams with an unmistakable inert marker in list/context output (e.g. [DREAM: not claimable — requires Erik's conversion]) so an agent reading the board sees both the idea and its status as un-actionable; (4) conversion 'update <id> --type item' is the authorization act and prints an explicit line saying the dream is now claimable work; (5) 'show' unchanged. WHY: verified 2026-07-28 that dream is convention only — orchestrator claimed a dream successfully and dreams appear in both list and the agent context blob, so an agent scanning the board can build one unasked. Rust tool: cargo build --release + cargo test.

title: DREAM: agent-handoff — successor briefing assembled from live state
description: Chris's idea 2026-07-28, working name agent-handoff. The ritual he does by hand: paste end-of-session chats + state-of-things into a new orchestrator ('you are a new project agent... review manna, review handoffs, review intent, tell me where we are and where we're headed'). Two halves: ASSEMBLY (build the successor brief) and CAPTURE (per-session narrative). Orchestrator's read: assembly needs NO new storage for v1 — manna context + coord status/history + zpc inject/patterns + git log since last handoff + agent-sessions summaries already contain the state of things; the brief is a bounded render of those, plus the reader preamble. Capture (session-end journal entry, the narrative arc zpc deliberately doesn't keep) is the real new object and belongs on the SessionEnd hook. TAXONOMY GATE: whether this is a new tool or verbs on an existing domain (sessions/zpc) is Erik's ruling; do not build either way until converted. DECIDE LATER.

title: git: worktree add binds memory and board to the primary checkout
description: WHAT: 'agent-git worktree add' currently seeds ignored files (.env, .env.*, CLAUDE.local.md, .agent-do/worktree-seed) but leaves two silent traps: (1) .zpc/ is gitignored (.gitignore:36) so a fresh worktree has NO store, and the SessionStart auto-init shipped 2026-07-28 creates an empty one at the worktree toplevel — every lesson that lane writes dies when the worktree is removed; (2) manna resolves .manna relative to the checkout (tools/agent-manna/src/store.rs:17) with no path override, so each worktree carries its own copy of the tracked board and parallel claims diverge. FIX: on worktree add, bind the new tree's .zpc to the primary store (symlink or pointer honored by resolve_zpc_dir) and either point manna at the primary board or refuse with a message naming the divergence. Both must survive worktree removal without data loss. Verify: lesson written from inside a worktree is present in the primary store after 'worktree remove'; a claim made from a worktree is visible to the primary checkout. WHY: worktree isolation silently breaks the memory and coordination layers built 2026-07-27/28.

title: coord: name the remedy when contention means isolation
description: WHAT: coord already raises a contention interrupt when two writers claim overlapping paths (agent-coord v2 roles/territories). Extend the interrupt text to name the remedy explicitly — 'agent-do git worktree add <branch>' — and add the second trigger it cannot see today: a lane whose declared branch differs from the parent checkout's HEAD (one working tree holds one branch, so that case is mandatory isolation, not a preference). Nudge only, never block: same ladder as the enforcement trinity. Kill switch consistent with existing coord env conventions. WHY: whether to isolate should not depend on an agent's taste; coord holds the ownership truth, so it should say the remedy out loud. Orchestrator position stated 2026-08-03: ownership beats isolation for same-branch parallel work; evidence is the 2026-07-27/28 memory-OS build (12 lanes, one tree, zero clobbering).

title: docs: lane template states the isolation rule
description: WHAT: docs/LANE-PROMPT-TEMPLATE.md gains one line under the claim block: isolation is required when your branch differs from the parent checkout's HEAD or when your owned paths overlap another live lane's; otherwise stay in the shared tree and own your paths. Cite 'agent-do git worktree add' as the mechanism and the memory/board binding caveat (mn-68d471) so no lane invents its own workaround. Small docs edit; no code. WHY: the rule must reach the agents who read prompts, not only the orchestrator.

title: zpc write-nudge misreads a bound worktree
description: The Stop hook hooks/claude/agent-do-zpc-write-nudge.sh resolves the store cwd-only ([ -d .zpc ] at line 61, STATE_DIR at :64, zpc_line_count glob at :80). In a worktree bound by 'agent-git worktree add' (mn-68d471) that .zpc is a pointer directory: the hook counts 0 memory lines forever and writes its baseline into the stub, so from the second Stop on it nudges 'you changed code and wrote no memory' even when every lesson landed in the primary store. Not lossy, just wrong. FIX: follow the pointer for STATE_DIR and zpc_line_count only, keeping cwd for the git change detection (the code moved in the worktree, the memory lives in the primary) — same trust rules as tools/agent-zpc/lib/common.sh:_zpc_store_pointer_target. The position-nudge hook shares the cwd-only check but only tests existence, so it is unaffected.

title: zpc security: memory bindings live in AGENT_DO_HOME, not in the repo
description: WHAT: the worktree memory binding (80cff36) is a repo-resident pointer at .zpc/primary-store, honored by _zpc_store_pointer_target (tools/agent-zpc/lib/common.sh:9, resolution below). .zpc/ is gitignored so the pointer is normally untracked, but a repository can force-add one, and cloning that repo silently redirects where every session reads AND writes memory (uid check limits targets to stores this user owns — including other projects' stores — so cross-project context injection and misdirected writes are both reachable with zero user action, since session-start injection is automatic). Repository content must never carry authority over where memory lives. FIX (preferred): keep bindings in a user-owned registry under $AGENT_DO_HOME keyed by absolute worktree path, written by 'agent-git worktree add', resolved by zpc; repo-resident pointers stop being honored. MINIMUM: refuse any pointer that git tracks (git ls-files --error-unmatch) AND require a matching registry entry. Keep the existing uid/ownership checks and the bounded walk; planted-store regressions must still pass. SOURCE: automated security review 2026-08-03, MEDIUM.

title: zpc security: a tracked .zpc store injects a repo's own text as project memory
description: ADJACENT to mn-84b9dc, found while closing it, NOT introduced by it. .zpc/ is gitignored in this repo but nothing stops any other repository from tracking .zpc/memory/lessons.jsonl. On clone it is a directory the cloning user owns, so the store walk accepts it and the session-start hook injects its contents under a heading that tells the agent this is the project's recorded truth (hooks/claude/agent-do-session-start.sh, append_zpc_memory). Repo content still becomes agent instructions; mn-84b9dc only closed the redirection half (a repo can no longer point at ANOTHER store). SCOPE: this is a design decision, not a bug fix — tests/test_worktree_binding.py::test_binding_is_bounded currently asserts a tracked store IS respected, on the reading that memory travelling with a branch is legitimate. Options: (a) keep, documented; (b) refuse stores git tracks (git ls-files --error-unmatch), which breaks the deliberate tracked-store case; (c) accept tracked stores but mark injected content as untrusted in the hook's heading. Erik picks.

title: hooks: stamp now on every turn (the temporal anchor)
description: WHAT: UserPromptSubmit hook injects one line per turn: absolute ISO local timestamp + weekday, elapsed since previous turn, elapsed since session start. Bounded (~1 line, <=120 chars), silent exit 0 on any failure, kill switch AGENT_DO_NOW=0, registered via install.sh CLAUDE_SETTINGS_SPECS + uninstall list; codex parity if its prompt hook supports injection. WHY: a model gets one clock reading at session start and then does date arithmetic against stale context — verified failure 2026-08-03: this orchestrator wrote '2026-07-28' into issues and lane prompts it created ON 2026-08-03, six days off, while proposing this very fix. Per-turn stamps also leave a trail of real 'now' moments in the transcript, so references to previous moments become readable instead of guessed.

title: zpc+manna: dated records render their age, so nobody does the arithmetic
description: WHAT: everywhere the system injects or lists dated records, render the age beside the date: '2026-07-27 (7d ago)'. Surfaces: zpc inject (lessons, patterns, corrections, preferences slice), zpc position/counsel output, manna list/show/context. Rendering happens at output time from the stored ISO timestamp; stored data is unchanged. WHY: models copy phrases reliably and compute date deltas unreliably. Existing proof: agent-coord already renders 'last_seen 3m ago' and its ages are never misreported, unlike bare-date records. Bound: age strings must not push inject past its existing char bounds.

title: DREAM: a time surface for on-demand truth (now/since/render)
description: Third piece of the 2026-08-03 temporal design, parked because it is a taxonomy ruling only Erik makes: whether 'now', 'since <ts>', 'render <ts>' (returns the correct English phrase for a delta) live as a new tool or as verbs on an existing domain. Pieces 1 and 2 (per-turn stamp mn-2895c2, pre-rendered ages mn-1da238) cover recorded records and the live conversation; this covers the residual case where an agent must produce a relative phrase for something not already rendered, and should ask instead of inventing. Honest limit of the whole design, worth restating here: it makes references to RECORDED events correct; it cannot fix a vague 'we discussed this recently' about something never recorded, except insofar as the per-turn stamp covers the conversation itself. DECIDE LATER — no agent executes this.
